---
title: "Fonts"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.2,
  dpi = 72,
  out.width = "100%",
  fig.showtext = TRUE
)
# downloaded Google Fonts go to a temporary folder while building this article, not to the user cache
Sys.setenv(R_USER_CACHE_DIR = tempdir())
```

```{r}
library(plot2)
```

`plot2()` can use any font that is installed on the system, and any of the fonts of [Google Fonts](https://fonts.google.com). Fonts other than the default font of the graphics device require the packages `showtext`, `showtextdb` and `sysfonts`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("showtext", "showtextdb", "sysfonts"))
```

## Setting a font

The `font` argument sets the font of all text in the plot. A Google Font that is not installed is downloaded once, the first time it is used:

```{r}
admitted_patients |>
  plot2(x = hospital,
        y = n(),
        category = gender,
        font = "Source Sans 3",
        title = "Admissions per hospital")
```

The font is used only while the plot is drawn, so other plots in the session are not affected.

## Downloaded fonts

Downloaded fonts are stored in the user cache folder of `plot2`, which `tools::R_user_dir("plot2", "cache")` returns. Fonts that have not been used for 90 days are removed from this folder automatically, so it does not grow over time.

## The same font for all plots

The option `plot2.font` sets the font for all plots in the session. Together with `plot2.text_factor`, which scales all text, this gives a consistent style, for example for a report:

```{r}
options(plot2.font = "Roboto Slab", plot2.text_factor = 1.1)

mtcars |>
  plot2(x = wt, y = mpg, title = "Fuel consumption and weight")
```

```{r}
options(plot2.font = NULL, plot2.text_factor = NULL)
```

## R Markdown and Quarto

In R Markdown and Quarto, `showtext` must render the text of the plot. Set the chunk option `fig.showtext = TRUE` (R Markdown) or `fig-showtext: true` (Quarto) in every chunk that uses another font, or once for the whole document:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.showtext = TRUE)
```

Without this option, `plot2()` stops with an error that explains how to set it.
